publication.title: Three-dimensional graph reconstruction of filamentous structures from z-stack images
publication.article_license: open access; confirm exact Creative Commons variant before reusing article figures

software_release.title: Three-dimensional graph reconstruction of filamentous structures from z-stack images: Code and data
software_release.software_license: MIT-style license as stated in Zenodo record

algorithm_steps: per-focal-plane filament detection and binary skeleton extraction
dense skeleton to sparse homeomorphic graph
optimal matching of node coordinates across focal planes
steerable-filter / orientation analysis for shallow overlaps

reported_results_to_reproduce.printed_filament_geometry: RMSE below 0.5 mm filament radius for most prototypes
reported_results_to_reproduce.human_intervention: Some branch/crossing cases require manual adjudication; the Zenodo record documents an additional false negative for crossing in image o.jpg.

human_assistance.documented_false_negative: image o.jpg top-right crossing; original configuration misses this and asks user to add one false negative manually

future_dataset.described_publication: Bright-Field Microscopy Dataset of Fungal Filament Networks for Detection, Focus Modeling, and 3D Reconstruction

claim_ceiling: The comparator is source-specific bright-field Z-stack graph reconstruction for Rhizophagus irregularis and 3D-printed prototypes. It includes manual crossing corrections and does not validate true biological anastomosis, transport or soil-scale 3D topology.
